{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took the top line from where it stopped near the middle of the body and carried it out to the nose, laying about 22 dominoes over four batches. That finished the upper outline of the fish and gave the head its shape. I also stood back up the few dominoes that fell near the nose and closed a small gap at the tip, so the head was in place before the push.

Execution: I inspected the body, the belly and the nose several times. I confirmed the doubled belly section was connected and would fall with the start, and I reported that to the table. When Hana asked me to run the top line to the nose, I did it in short batches and checked each one before the next. I kept my last fixes light, as Sofia asked, and went hands-off before time was called.

Collaboration: I kept to my assigned area, the nose and top line. I stayed off the tail and the bottom line when asked, and I confirmed the plan out loud so we never doubled up on a stroke. I gave regular short updates on what I could see and what I was about to lay, and I offered to hand the top line back when Hana wanted it. I also backed the fish idea quickly so we could start building.

Leadership: I kept the mood light and the table energised during the long stretch of waiting and checking. I called out the time and the hands-off point so everyone stopped touching the build before the push. I spoke up early with clear, honest status reports, which helped the table make decisions quickly.

Overall, I completed the stretch I was given and did the final nose check. I believe my share of the result was about a quarter, alongside the design and the bottom line that others built.", "my_share_percent": 25}
